We need an explanation and an immediate mitigation — the C-suite is already asking questions. Can someone join a hot call now?

Quick technical summary from infra traces and a local repro:
- We observed repeated "incomplete-header" and "stream-parser-exit" errors in the serving runtime logs for BrightCheckout tenant ID during 08:40–09:05 PT.
- Traces show clients sending a sequence of small chunked frames with interleaved header metadata; our node-level dechunker occasionally emits fragmented header frames to the streaming parser. When that happens, the parser discards the partially reassembled header block and triggers a connection reset.
- Repro steps (local): hitting the endpoint with small chunk sizes + aggressive keepalive produces identical resets. This aligns with the customer's "stream stalled" symptom.

Suggested immediate mitigations (short term):
1) Route BrightCheckout traffic to the less aggressive parser variant that tolerates fragmented headers (config flip on routing policy) — low risk, immediate.
2) Deploy a hotfix to the dechunker that buffers header fragments until complete (requires a short patch and can be shipped behind a canary in Dedicated).
3) Ask the customer to temporarily increase client chunk size to 8k as a temporary band-aid (we'll provide a code snippet).

Attachments: parser-trace-0824.json (application/json), mitigation-playbook-0824.md (text/markdown)

I'll start the routing flip now and push a canary for the dechunker patch if the flip doesn't stabilize errors.

- Priyom
Senior SWE, Serving Runtime
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Laura Jenkins <laura.jenkins@brightcheckout.com>, Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@brightcheckout.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: BrightCheckout incident update and executive next steps

Laura & Samir — thank you for the quick report and patience. Short executive summary for your leadership:

- Impact: Intermittent checkout failures affecting ~30% sessions, elevated error rate (~12%), and p99 latency increase from ~350ms to ~5s between 08:40–09:05 PT.
- Root cause (preliminary): Client-server streaming interaction exposed a header reassembly edge case in our dechunker + parser pipeline. Under specific small-chunk patterns the parser would drop partial header frames and reset the connection.
- Immediate actions taken by Redwood: routing flip to a tolerant parser variant (started 12:20 PT), guard-canary pushed for dechunker buffer fix (in-progress), suggested temporary client-side chunk-size increase and provided mitigation playbook.
- Next steps: complete canary and full rollout for dechunker patch (ETA 24 hours), share post-incident RCA and regression tests, coordinate a joint follow-up to harden SDK and provide a recommended config.

We'd like to set a 30-minute exec call today at 17:00 PT to walk through the timeline and the remediation plan. Rishi will send calendar invite. Please reply if that time doesn't work.

Apologies for the disruption — we take this seriously and will prioritize a durable fix and test coverage to prevent recurrence.

Best,
